correctness.rationale: On the aligned dyadic path of length 2^d, an ancestor-closed mask spans, with the constant, exactly the block-constant functions of its leaf partition. Block averaging takes a unit monotone step to a monotone vector in [0,1], and decomposition into steps gives contractivity. A step between leaves is fixed for every nonempty closed mask, and the empty mask maps to constants. If I is retained and its parent J is absent, the midpoint step of I has a retained detail -1/2,+1/2 on the two halves of I, zero on the sibling. All other retained nonzero details are ancestors constant on J. The midpoint and sibling edges of J contribute 1 and 1/2, independently of all other edges. For a root-child singleton mask, the one internal jump and one exterior interface give V(h_I)=3/sqrt(|I|), and its largest step coefficient is sqrt(|I|)/2; the step decomposition proves the matching upper bound. At d=1 there are no nonclosed masks.
residual_risks: The all-depth result rests on the mathematical proof. Frozen exact mask exhaustion is only through depth four, with the separate isolated-child witness checked through depth nine.

value.rationale: Fixed mask selection is a natural linear model for the Haar/TV stability question. Knowing exactly which masks can safely be used matters beyond knowing that globally bad examples exist; a dimension-free quantitative obstruction for every forbidden mask, witnessed by a single explicit step for that mask, is a substantive structural result.
residual_risks: No exact norm is given for all nonclosed masks, nor any assertion about nonbinary paths, weights, cycles or nonlinear thresholding.
